title: Idriss Déby Overthrows Hissène Habré in Armed Coup
note: Déby's MPS forces entered N'Djamena on 1 December 1990, overthrowing Habré after an offensive from Sudan. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Movement for Democracy and Development Rebellion Begins
note: Southern rebellions did occur against Déby's early regime but no specific Wikipedia article confirms the Movement for Democracy and Development by name in 1991; plausible but no direct source found.

title: Sovereign National Conference Convened
note: The Sovereign National Conference ran 15 January–7 April 1993 and produced the Transitional Charter. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: CFA Franc Devaluation Doubles Import Costs
note: CFA franc devalued 50% on 12 January 1994, doubling import costs. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum
note: Constitutional referendum held 31 March 1996; approved by ~61% of voters. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Déby Wins First Multiparty Presidential Election
note: Déby defeated Kamougué in a second-round runoff on 3 July 1996 with ~69% of the vote. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: MDJT Rebellion Erupts in Tibesti Mountains
note: Youssouf Togoïmi formed the MDJT on 12 October 1998 and launched armed insurgency from the Tibesti region. Year, leader, and location confirmed.

title: World Bank Approves Chad-Cameroon Pipeline Revenue Plan
note: World Bank approved the pipeline project on 6 June 2000 with an unprecedented revenue management framework. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Déby Re-elected in Disputed Second Term
note: Déby won with ~63% on 20 May 2001; six opposition candidates alleged massive fraud and were briefly arrested. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Darfur Conflict Spills Over into Eastern Chad
note: Darfur conflict began February 2003; ~200,000 Sudanese refugees fled to eastern Chad by late 2003; Janjaweed cross-border raids documented. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: First Crude Oil Exported via Chad-Cameroon Pipeline
note: First crude oil loaded on 3 October 2003 from the FSO vessel offshore Kribi, Cameroon. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Failed Military Coup Attempt Against Déby
note: Coup attempt foiled on the night of 16 May 2004; ~80 rebels including Colonel Bechir Haggar arrested. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Constitutional Referendum Abolishes Presidential Term Limits
note: Referendum held 6 June 2005; approved removal of two-term presidential limit by 66% of voters. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Chad Breaks World Bank Oil Revenue Agreement
note: The petroleum revenue law was amended in December 2005, but the World Bank suspended lending in early January 2006 — the break and World Bank response occurred in 2006, not 2005. Year is partially misleading: the law change was late 2005 but the Bank's suspension/public rupture was January 2006. However as the law amendment itself was December 2005, this is borderline; the description says the World Bank suspended lending 'in response' implying 2005 is the year of the break — core framing is accurate enough but the World Bank suspension happened in 2006.

title: Rebels Attack N'Djamena — State of Emergency Declared
note: FUC/UFDC attacked N'Djamena on 13 April 2006 and was repelled. A state of emergency declaration is less clearly documented for this specific attack (more clearly documented for the 2008 attack), but the assault and repulsion are confirmed. Minor note.

title: Déby Wins Third Term Amid Opposition Boycott
note: Déby won a third presidential term in 2006 after the main opposition boycotted; EU declined to send observers. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Humanitarian Crisis Deepens in Eastern Chad
note: UN authorized EUFOR Chad/CAR via resolution 1778 of 25 September 2007 to protect civilians in eastern Chad. Displacement figures for 2007 are plausible. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Second Major Rebel Assault on N'Djamena
note: Coalition rebels entered N'Djamena on 2 February 2008, reached near the presidential palace; French forces aided evacuation. Hundreds of casualties reported. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: EUFOR Chad/CAR Peacekeeping Mission Deploys
note: EUFOR deployed from February 2008; authorized strength was 4,300 (3,700 deployed + 600 reserve). Event says 3,700 which matches deployed force. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: MINURCAT Takes Over UN Peacekeeping in Eastern Chad
note: MINURCAT assumed authority from EUFOR on 15 March 2009; mission terminated 31 December 2010 at Chad's request. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Chad-Sudan Rapprochement Ends Proxy War
note: Rapprochement agreement signed 15 January 2010; joint border patrols deployed and border reopened in April 2010. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Déby Wins Fourth Term with 89% of Vote
note: Déby won 89% after major opposition boycotted the April 2011 election. Year and core facts confirmed (minor variation in one source citing 83.6%, but majority of sources confirm ~89%).

title: Chad Deploys Troops to Mali Intervention
note: Chad deployed 2,000 troops as the largest African contributor to Operation Serval; Chadian forces suffered significant casualties in Adrar des Ifoghas. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Multinational Joint Task Force Reactivated Against Boko Haram
note: Lake Chad countries committed 8,000+ troops to MNJTF in late 2014/early 2015; AU authorized the force March 2015. The reactivation/restructuring began in 2014. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Boko Haram Launches Suicide Bombings in N'Djamena
note: Bombings on 15 June and 11 July 2015 killed 33 and 15 people respectively; Chad banned full-face veils immediately after. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Lake Chad Shrinks to Fraction of Historic Size
note: Lake Chad lost ~90% of its surface area from 1963 peak (~26,000 km²) to less than 1,500 km²; impact on 10+ million people across four countries confirmed. Event assigns year 2015 as reference point, which is valid for an ongoing crisis. Core facts confirmed.

title: Déby Wins Fifth Term — Opposition Leader Arrested
note: Déby won 59.92% in 2016 election; Kebzabo came second (not arrested — he rejected results). Description says 'opposition leader arrested' but sources show post-election crackdown on protests, not Kebzabo's arrest. Minor factual imprecision but year and election result confirmed.

title: Severe Austerity Amid Oil Price Collapse
note: Oil price collapse since 2014 forced severe austerity; civil servant salary cuts, teacher and healthcare strikes documented through 2017-2018. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: New Constitution Establishes Fourth Republic
note: President Déby promulgated the 2018 constitution on 4 May 2018, abolishing the prime minister position and creating a presidential system. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: US Includes Chad in Travel Ban Then Reverses
note: Chad added to US travel ban 24 September 2017; ban lifted effective 13 April 2018. Event year of 2018 refers to the reversal — slightly ambiguous but the reversal year is correct. Core facts confirmed.

title: Boko Haram Kills 98 Chadian Soldiers at Bohoma
note: Attack occurred 23 March 2020; casualty figures vary by source (92 per Al Jazeera, 98 per US State Dept); Déby launched Operation Bohoma Anger in retaliation. Year and core facts confirmed with minor discrepancy in casualty count.

title: FACT Rebel Column Invades from Southern Libya
note: FACT entered Chad from Libya on election day 11 April 2021 and advanced hundreds of kilometers; directly caused Déby's death on 20 April 2021. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Compounds Humanitarian Crisis
note: Chad declared state of health emergency in 2020; pandemic disrupted humanitarian access. Plausible and consistent with documented global COVID-19 responses. Year confirmed.

title: France Launches Operation Barkhane Strike from Chad
note: Operation Barkhane was headquartered in N'Djamena throughout its operation including 2020; France had approximately 1,000 troops in Chad. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Déby Killed on Frontline — Transitional Military Council Formed
note: Idriss Déby died 20 April 2021 from battle wounds; son Mahamat Idriss Déby took power via Transitional Military Council, dissolving parliament and constitution. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Security Forces Kill Protesters Opposing Military Takeover
note: Security forces killed at least 5–13 people (sources vary) during April-May 2021 protests; the event claims 'at least 13' which is on the higher end of estimates. Core facts confirmed.

title: African Union and France Endorse Transitional Council
note: AU and France gave de facto endorsement to the Transitional Military Council citing regional security priorities; AU called for 18-month transition to civilian rule. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Deadly Crackdown on Pro-Democracy Protests — Black Thursday
note: On 20 October 2022 security forces killed at least 50 protesters (National Human Rights Commission cited 128 killed); event called 'Black Thursday'. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: National Dialogue Boycotted by Key Opposition Groups
note: National dialogue concluded 8 October 2022; FACT and major opposition groups boycotted; transition extended two years; Mahamat Déby allowed to run in elections. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: France Begins Barkhane Withdrawal — Sahel Realignment
note: France completed withdrawal from Mali and ended Operation Barkhane in 2022; maintained base in N'Djamena. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: New Constitution Approved — Fifth Republic Established
note: Constitutional referendum held 17 December 2023; 'yes' won with 86%; Fifth Republic designation and decentralized system confirmed. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Wagner Group Influence Expands in Neighboring States
note: Wagner active in CAR, Sudan, and Libya in 2023; US intelligence shared with Chadian government about Wagner destabilization plots. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Lake Chad Basin Displacement Exceeds 3 Million
note: IOM data for 2023 shows over 6 million total affected individuals across four countries; the '3 million' figure appears to refer only to IDPs/refugees (not returnees), which is plausible but the headline number is an undercount of total displacement. Figure is plausible but exact 3-million threshold for the stated year cannot be precisely confirmed.

title: Mahamat Déby Wins Presidential Election with 61%
note: Election held 6 May 2024; Mahamat Déby won with 61% of the vote; Succès Masra came second with 18.54% and initially rejected results. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Chad Terminates Defense Cooperation Agreement with France
note: Chad announced termination of the defense cooperation agreement on 28–29 November 2024, ordering withdrawal of French troops. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Sudanese Civil War Drives Massive Refugee Influx
note: Sudan war began April 2023; by late 2024 over 720,000 new Sudanese refugees entered Chad; total Sudan-related displacement exceeded 1.2 million in Chad. '700,000 additional' figure is consistent with UNHCR data. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Chad Pivots Toward Russia and Turkey for Security
note: Following France departure, Chad engaged Russia (Déby visited Moscow January 2024) and Turkey (Abéché base deal January 2025); Gulf states engagement also confirmed. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: French Military Withdrawal from N'Djamena Completed
note: France handed over the Kossei base in N'Djamena on 30–31 January 2025, completing withdrawal from Chad after nearly 70 years of military presence. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Escalating Sahel Instability Threatens Chad's Borders
note: Ongoing instability in Sudan, Libya, and CAR is well-documented through 2024; the 2025 characterization is plausible and consistent with trends but specific 2025 events cannot be independently verified given the nature of the claim.
